The ACP, Yeshwanthapura police station, has submitted charge sheet against the accused for the offence punishable U/s.498A, 304(B) of IPC and Section.3 and 4 of D.P.Act in Crime No.352/2018 Peenya Ps vs Pratheep S on 23 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106055942/

sentences.text:
The brief story of the prosecution are as under:
The marriage of accused and deceased Manuja was performed at Koppa village,
Mandya District, as per the customs prevailed in their community.
At the time of marriage, the accused on demand received cash of Rs.50,000/- and gold articles as dowry.
After marriage, they started to reside at Rajagopalanagar.
Due to marital relationship, the deceased has gave birth to a baby girl by name Rishika.
After sometime, the accused started to torture the deceased physically and mentally to bring remaining dowry amount of Rs.50,000/- and also additional dowry of Rs.70,000/-.

Due to the continuous physical and mental torture of the accused, the deceased unable to bear the torture and on 08.07.2018 at 2.00 p.m. at matrimonial house committed suicide by hanging herself and thereby the accused has committed the offences as alleged against him.
3. The concerned police have submitted charge sheet before the concerned ACMM., Bangalore.
The learned Magistrate has took cognizance of the offences and committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. after furnishing copy of charge sheet to the accused.
The same was numbered as SC No.1869/2018.
4. The prosecution has examined ten witnesses as PW.1 to PW.10 and got exhibited documents at Ex.P1 to P16.
On consent of the accused counsel, the inquest Mahazar and P.M.Report have been marked at Ex.P.11 and 12 respectively.
The learned PP has given up C.W.12 to 20.

The court has issued summons, warrant and proclamation against C.W.8, 9 and 11, the police failed to execute warrant and produce them before the court to record their evidence, as such the prayer of the learned PP was rejected and the witnesses CW.8, 9 and 11 were dropped.
However liberty has been given to the prosecution for examination of the said witnesses, if the said witnesses brought before the court by the concerned police before conclusion of trial.

5. After completion of prosecution side evidence, this Court has recorded the statement of accused,
as provided U/s.313 of Cr.P.C.
The accused has denied incriminating evidence present against him and not claimed any defense evidence nor submitted anything to the Court.
The accused has complied application u/s.437A of Cr.PC by executing personal bond and surety bond.

6. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials on record.
7.

The following points that arises for consideration of this court:
1. Whether the prosecution proves that the marriage of accused and deceased Manuja was performed at Koppa village, Mandya District, as per the customs prevailed in their community and at the time of marriage, the accused on demand received cash of Rs.50,000/- and gold articles as dowry, after marriage, they started to reside at Rajagopalanagar, due to marital relationship, the deceased has gave birth to a baby Peenya Ps vs Pratheep S on 23 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106055942/
2 girl by name Rishika, after sometime, the accused started to torture the deceased physically and mentally to bring remaining dowry amount of Rs.50,000/- and also additional dowry of Rs.70,000/- and thereby accused has committed the offence punishable U/s.3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961?

2. Whether the prosecution proves that the the marriage of accused and deceased Manuja was performed at Koppa Village, Mandya District as per the customs prevailed in their community and at the time of marriage, the accused on demand received cash of Rs.50,000/- and gold articles as dowry, after marriage, they started to reside at Rajagopalanagar, due to marital relationship, the deceased has gave birth to a baby girl by name Rishika, after sometime, the accused started to torture the deceased physically and mentally to bring remaining dowry amount of Rs.50,000/-
and also additional dowry of Rs.70,000/- and thereby accused has committed an offence punishable u/s 498A of IPC?
3. Whether the prosecution proves that accused subjected the deceased to physical and mental cruelty for additional dowry and due to such cruelty and harassment forced the deceased to commit suicide by hanging herself on 08.07.2018 at 2.00 p.m.
in her matrimonial house and thereby accused has committed offence of dowry death punishable U/s.304B of IPC?
4. What order?
8. This Court has answered the above above points are as under:
 Point No.1: In the Negative  Point No.2: In the Negative  Point No.3: In the Negative  Point No.4: As per final order  for the following:
 R E A S O N S 9.
Points Nos.1 to 3: These points are taken up together as they are related to each other and to avoid repetition in the discussion.

The prosecution examined the parents of the deceased Manuja by name Govindachari and Bhagyamma as P.W.1 and P.W.2 respectively and got marked complaint, spot Mahazar, marriage invitation and photos at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.4.
Further the statement of P.W.1 and statement of P.W.2 have been marked at Ex.P.5 to Ex.P.7.
The evidence of P.W.1 and 2 proves that the marriage of deceased Manuja with accused were performed at Koppa.

After marriage, they were living together Peenya Ps vs Pratheep S on 23 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106055942/
3 happily.
Due to marital relationship, the deceased had gave birth to a child by name Rishika.

Except the said evidence, nothing has been deposed to believe the accused has tortured the deceased physically and mentally by demanding additional dowry and due to the continuous torture of the accused, the deceased has committed suicide at her matrimonial house.
It is no doubt, the complaint and spot Mahazar have been marked at Ex.P.1 and 2.
But the evidence given by the father P.W.1 is not in accordance with the recitals of the complaint and Mahazar.
Even the mother of the deceased Bhagyamma also not supported the prosecution story by deposing contrary evidence to her statement.
10. It is pertinent to note that the prosecution also examined the relatives of the deceased by name Srinivas, Kalavathi, Shilpa, Anand Kumar and Girish as P.W.3 to P.W.7 respectively.
The said witnesses being the relatives categorically deposed about the marriage between the deceased and the accused.
Even according to the evidence of the said witnesses, both deceased and accused were leading happy marital life.
Except that, nothing has been deposed related to the physical and mental harassment received by the deceased from the accused.
As such the learned PP has treated the P.W.1 to P.W.7 as hostile and cross-examined.

Inspite of the efforts of the learned PP, failed to bring out any worthful evidence to consider the accused has tortured the deceased for dowry and due to the continuous torture, the deceased has committed suicide.
As such, the statements of the said witnesses P.W.3 to 7 marked at Ex.P.8 to Ex.P.10, Ex.P.13 and Ex.P.14 respectively.

It is no doubt the inquest Mahazar and P.M.Report marked with consent of the accused at Ex.P.11 and Ex.P.12,
perhaps the oral testimony of the parents and relatives of the deceased not at all supports the case of the prosecution to consider that the deceased has committed suicide due to the torture of the accused for dowry.

As such, no much importance has been given to the Ex.P.11 and Ex.P.12.
11.
It is necessary to note that pancha by name Sampath examined as P.W.8 identified his signature present on spot Mahazar Ex.P.2.
But the said witness not able to give evidence in accordance with the conducting of Mahazar by Investigation Officer.

As such, the learned PP has treated the said witness as hostile, but not succeeded to get any worthful evidence to believe conducting of Mahazar by the Investigation Officer P.W.10 in his presence at spot.
12. It is obvious to note that the witness P.W.9 Srinivas being the PI has registered the FIR vide 352/2018 as per Ex.P.15.

He went to the spot immediately and shifted the dead body of the deceased to Sapthagiri hospital with the assistance of the police staff and also sent requisition to the concerned through C.W.16 to conduct inquest Mahazar on the dead body of the deceased.
Thereafter handed over further investigation to P.W.10 Raviprasad.

The said witness P.W.10 being the ACP after receiving further investigation, on the same day visited the spot and conducted Mahazar as per Ex.P.2 in the presence of the panchas and prepared rough sketch as per Ex.P.16.

On the same day,
the accused was produced before him.
He has carried out arrest procedure against the accused and recorded his voluntary statement and thereafter produced before the court alongwith remand application.
He has recorded statement of the witnesses and further statement of the complainant.
He has collected the inquest report and P.M.Report and also the clothes of the deceased.

He has brought the said clothes of the deceased into P.F.No.119/2018 and submitted to the court and on 12.09.2018 he has collected the marriage invitation and photos of the deceased and accused and thereafter submitted charge sheet against the accused.

The evidence given by the police witness Peenya Ps vs Pratheep S on 23 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106055942/
4 P.W.9 and P.W.10 has completely denied by the accused counsel.
It is very clear from the above discussion that the evidence of the Investigation Officers not match or corroborate with the evidence of parents and relatives of the deceased.
It is very clear that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt against the accused.
As such, this court has answered the Point Nos.1 and 2 in the Negative.
13. Point No.3:

In view of answer of this court on points No.1 and 2, this court proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 304(B) of IPC and Section.3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
The bail bond and surety bond of accused stands cancelled.
(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcript corrected by me and then pronounced in open Court on this the 23 rd day of February, 2026)
(E. RAJEEVA GOWDA) XLV Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru
